The class directly subclasses logging.FileHandler. handleError is the required standard-library callback invoked by emit after a write failure; renaming it would restore stderr tracebacks and lose failed_writes accounting. A real handler write failure preserves the existing file, increments once, emits no stderr, and a subsequent write succeeds.

This pair compares the connection-definition content hash and declared connector implementation revision against the approved snapshot before opening a connection. Neither token is a stored-format version. Stale binding, remote schema change, real crash and actual effect assertions remain enforced.

The current definition content hash is rechecked under the owner lock before publishing discovered Tools, together with the connector revision. Concurrent changes must preserve the prior catalog and all current Project bytes without Tool/model calls. This is a publication CAS, not format negotiation.

The catalog snapshot content hash and connector revision must still match the current connection definition and adapter. Stale discovery is rejected and explicit preparation is required; no old-format Reader is selected.

The target public snapshot version is its content-change token, compared to the explicitly pinned Skill resource revision. Target changes are rejected until the caller updates the reference; this is the preserved revision contract, not a schema version branch.

Run/Step activity source references forbid component/version fields altogether. This None test enforces that ownership variant, not supported storage-version values. Otherwise-valid JSON with a forbidden reference field is rejected by the actual activity Reader without rewriting or leaking stored evidence.

expected_version is the reviewed recovery-plan content token. Recompute and compare the plan before creating a recovery journal or applying any repair; changed source evidence must reject the request rather than guess history. Current docs explicitly preserve this CAS name.

expected_version is the reviewed retention-plan token over current sources, not a format version. Compare a fresh plan before validating selected targets and pruning. Same-size/mtime source mutation rejects the stale request and preserves all original history bytes; rollback and process-death tests remain intact.

The Tool package snapshot content token is checked before disabling the selected Tool; deletion then passes the same expected_version to the backend owner CAS. The stale command keeps the enabled package and valid deletion preserves the original import source. No schema version branch is involved.

The built-in Component settings snapshot token rejects stale UI commands before changing the enabled list; the backend configure API enforces the token again. The integration also exercises saved selection, approval, actual file effect and reopen. This is a configuration CAS, not a format comparison.

The condition rejects a missing close_timeout attribute or a supplied non-finite/non-positive/non-numeric deadline. It never supplies a default; explicit None is retained. Registration validation precedes session creation and closing one timed-out processor does not skip others.

This rejection predicate checks the declared retry_fields tuple, nonempty string entries and uniqueness. An explicitly empty tuple is valid and remains empty. It does not synthesize retry policy or replace stored missing fields; the closed Reader and registry revalidation remain mandatory.

Under the explicit non-None branch, this condition rejects boolean, non-finite and non-positive supplied deadlines; math.isfinite rejects nonnumeric objects. It is validation, not a value fallback. The actual timed-out step is finalized as failed and its coroutine is closed.

This guard requires unique string retry node identifiers and exact equality with the uncertain node set before resume. It rejects an inconsistent explicit selection; it does not fill a missing selection or clear effect/checkpoint evidence. Explicit retry and duplicate-resume rejection remain tested.

The condition returns early only for the validated boolean enabled/log_reads switches. It never replaces False with True or creates a missing configuration value. LogConfig rejects non-booleans; normal logging appends without implicit retention or duplicate handlers.

This is the supplied max_delay numeric/finite/positive validation predicate. Invalid values are rejected, not changed to a default. Actual timer and cancellation flushes protect accepted output independently of the predicate classification.

This predicate rejects a retry_safe_tools value that is not a tuple of nonempty strings; explicit empty tuples stay empty. It does not grant retry admission or erase uncertain effects. The referenced real-effect test proves that an admitted retry cannot convert a prior uncertain receipt into no-effect evidence; it is not claimed as exhaustive invalid-input coverage.

Under an explicit non-None branch this guard rejects boolean, non-numeric, non-finite and non-positive deadlines. No truthy replacement or hidden deadline is introduced. Optional deadline/cancellation and preserved failure/effect evidence are verified at the actual executor boundary.

After blocked/backend-admitted/access checks, this condition combines no-effect evidence and the supplied retry-safe fact to choose a UI recovery action. It does not substitute a retry policy or authorize the backend. Only already backend-admitted Tools are eligible for retry selection.

This condition chooses which settings widgets are visible when a search query is present or the policy tab is selected. Its result is consumed only as a condition; no query, policy or stored setting is replaced. Categorized editing and project-scoped save/reload behavior remain exercised.

This prefix/config-path condition only determines whether a form help description is added. It does not determine a configuration value or collapse Missing/Null/Value. Missing/null/nested/unknown settings preservation and shared-key engine-lock consumers remain tested.

Zero is the mathematical lower boundary of the owner-declared technical cache capacity. Zero disables caching, positive capacities only evict derived projections, and negative/non-integer inputs are rejected. It is not a domain execution or retention limit. Actual file tests preserve authoritative bytes and identity/version rejection; Run/Step repositories consume FileCatalog.DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES as their single sizing declaration.

This condition permits reuse only inside matching content and preparation-fingerprint checks, when the prior graph is complete or extraction was explicitly disabled. It chooses an execution branch; it does not replace the graph flag, extraction policy or missing configuration. The owner separately validates stored document graph_complete as boolean. Reuse, changed preparation and real model receipt assertions remain mandatory.

This predicate classifies allowed graph-validation/provider failures only under the explicit best_effort extraction policy. Other exceptions propagate. No retry/extraction default is constructed, and quota, storage and cancellation protections are not approved away. The S3 error-code declarations and S6 Provider audit remain separate candidates.

The conditional re-raises after any received stream item or when the owning retry policy disallows another attempt. It combines an observation and a boolean policy decision; no value is defaulted and no retry budget is reset. SDK retry ownership and no retry after a partial delta remain tested.

The condition identifies a timeout exception by type or class name. It selects a diagnostic classification and never supplies a configuration value or execution deadline. This S2 judgment does not waive separate SDK/wire ownership or error-code declaration work.

retry is a fact attached to an already observed Tool execution, not a retry policy. Its False default means the caller did not label that observation a retry. This owner only updates transient counters/recent facts and isolates sink errors; it does not authorize, retry, persist receipts or impose execution limits.

The condition determines whether configured Project or Run limits require reading prior/auxiliary usage. has_limit returns a boolean from explicit non-None limits. No policy, usage record or reservation is replaced. Unlimited calls still retain receipts and bounded calls keep their independent cumulative evidence.

This condition selects auxiliary usage reads when an explicit Project limit exists or an owning Run has a limit. Source ownership and active-Run validation occur before the branch; the boolean expression does not create a fallback policy or erase a receipt. Reservation occurs before the model effect and cancelled/unknown usage remains accounted.

The expression is consumed only as the condition for token counting: an explicit Project token limit, or a Run source with an explicit Run token limit. It does not select a replacement limit or coerce a missing receipt to zero. Required counters, nonnegative counts, reserved unknown usage and actual call limits remain enforced by their owners.

The public API alone owns the default False for an explicit retry command. Omission permits an ordinary queued Job but never authorizes retrying a failed or interrupted Job. RAGJobs.run requires this argument and rejects every non-bool before lease acquisition, state writes or model effects. This command neither supplies provider retry policy nor bypasses revision, abandonment, checkpoint or usage checks. Actual model-effect counts and all Project file bytes are asserted for invalid inputs, and explicit True is verified with the current resume-plan revision.
